messages:
maria_support: @channel heads-up — customer ClipperAI reporting elevated p95 for streaming completions starting ~2034560000. They see lots of client retries and intermittent 504s from our gateway. They've throttled to avoid billing blowup but want an update.
kevin_w: Can you paste a minimal repro? SDK version, region, whether they use chunked streaming or SSE, and any error snippets from their side?
maria_support: They use our JS SDK v0.9.1 with streaming (chunked). Customer paste: `STREAM_ERR: 504 gateway_timeout (after 15s)` and sometimes `502 upstream_reset` in client logs. They say p95 went from ~600ms -> 4s for chunks. Also: heavy retry loop on their side — they set retries to 5.
ajson_prod: Uploading their repro steps (from customer):

```
# repro steps
1) open streaming request to /v1/streams with Authorization Bearer <token>
2) keep connection open ~30s and let server stream tokens
3) at ~10-20s they rotate token locally (background refresher) which closes underlying socket
4) client restarts request immediately (no backoff)
```

Logs:
```
client: socket closed -> reconnect
server: 2023-11-12T10:23:12Z gateway: upstream reset
gateway: responded 502/504 to client
```

They also shared our SDK debug output showing `H2 connection reused` then `reset_stream` after token refresh.
sara_eng: That pattern screams connection recycling when auth rotates mid-stream. If the SDK doesn't handle token refresh gracefully for long-lived streaming, the client will hammer new connections -> upstream queue pressure -> gateway timeouts. We saw similar in a past keepalive bug.
amelia_ops: Also check our edge proxy idle/keepalive times and HTTP/2 GOAWAY behavior. If the edge sends GOAWAY on token change or connection reset, remaining in-flight streams may be aborted and retried by the client.
kevin_w: Can we pull ingress+egress logs for that customer's requests (trace id if available)? Need proxy-level upstream timings, queue depth, and worker backpressure metrics. Maria, can you ask them for a sample trace-id? If they don't have one, we'll correlate by timestamp range.
maria_support: Asked for trace-id. Meanwhile customer provided one sample: trace=ci-clipper-2034567890-xyz

ops-bot: started log-collection job for trace ci-clipper-2034567890-xyz (job id jb-3344) :mag:

kevin_w: I pulled logs. Immediate observations:
- many short lived streams from same client IP within <1s windows
- gateway responded 502 for ~12% of aborted streams and 504 for timed-out requests when worker queue was saturated
- backend latency (model) stayed stable; issue appears at gateway/upstream handoff

kevin_w: Hypothesis: token refresh triggers abrupt socket closure; SDK restarts streams aggressively (no jitter/backoff); this creates short-lived spikes that exhaust gateway worker concurrency and manifest as 502/504 for unrelated users.

sara_eng: Quick mitigations we can try for the customer:
- ask them to downgrade retries to max 2 and add exponential backoff (jitter)
- enable SDK option `gracefulTokenRefresh: true` (they're on v0.9.1 — not enabled by default) or upgrade to v0.10.x which has better streaming token rollover
- temporarily increase gateway worker_pool and increase streaming idle timeout + keepalive on edge for their region

maria_support: Communicated mitigation steps to customer. They're willing to try SDK upgrade and lowering retries. They asked for a quick config change on our side if it helps while they deploy.

amelia_ops: I'll push a temporary route tweak for their tenant to increase edge keepalive to 60s and bump worker_pool for the next 30m to see if it reduces 502/504. Applying canary to eu-west first.

ops-bot: deploy started for route tweak -> route: tenant/clipperai; canary: eu-west; exp: 30m; user: amelia_ops

kevin_w: Also instrumented streaming route with a `token_refresh` annotation so we can correlate connection resets with auth events. Added high-cardinality tag `client_retry_count` to traces.

maria_support: Customer applied SDK change (downgraded retries=2 + jitter) and started a test. They report fewer retries and initial observation: p95 dropped from ~4.5s -> ~1.1s after SDK change/upgraded client. Still seeing occasional 502s (~1-2 per 100 requests).

kevin_w: Progress. Next steps:
- keep the canary for 60m and monitor 
- schedule a post-mortem if 502/504 persists after SDK upgrade
- create an internal runbook entry for streaming token rotation edge-case

sara_eng: Long-term engineering actions:
- make SDK token refresh graceful by default for streaming (queued handoff vs abort)
- add server-side soft-close window for token rotation so in-flight streams can finish a short period
- rate-limit rapid reconnects per IP/tenant to avoid retry storms

maria_support: Customer relieved but still wants a written timeline + root-cause analysis and assurance on billing impact. I'll draft customer-facing summary once we confirm canary results.

kevin_w: Adding a temporary billing credit offer (small) if they saw >X unexpected retries — coordinate with billing after we confirm invoice delta. @sara_eng can you estimate worst-case token-refresh retry amplification multiplier so we can ballpark credits?
sara_eng: Rough estimate based on their retry-5 -> 2 change: retry amplification could be ~3x requests during spike windows. I'll send a quick calc in the thread.

ops-bot: canary finished in eu-west: success (reduced 502/504 by ~70% for test window)

maria_support: Customer accepted mitigation and will roll SDK upgrade to prod tomorrow. Leaving this thread open until 2034568123 to confirm no regression. Preparing customer note and billing standby.

kevin_w: Filed follow-up issues:
- ENG-STREAM-1123: streaming token refresh graceful by default
- OPS-EDGE-7720: add soft-close window for auth rotation
- DOCS-55: streaming best-practices (retries/backoff, token rotation)

maria_support: Thanks everyone. I'll post final customer note and close when we verify no further 502/504s.

sara_eng: thx — good catch. :thumbsup:
